host: MacBookAir10,1 (M1, 8 GB), debug and release builds, synthetic inputs

inputs.500-page text PDF: 566 KB, ~14 text lines/page, one shared image every 25th page

before.500-page PDF (debug): 84.8 s; 681 MB written to checkpoint.json (full document re-serialized per page)
before.3000-page PDF: would fail: default 1000-unit limit and 120 s timeout; extrapolated ~509 s

after.500-page resume (debug): 0.46 s, all units reused, no Poppler calls
after.400k-row CSV (debug): 16.1 s wall including the 203 MB result write; extractor time 6.2 s
after.400k-row CSV (release): 2.97 s wall, ~537 MB sampled peak RSS, 203 MB result (11.9x input)
after.700k-row CSV (release): 3.25 s wall, ~932 MB sampled peak RSS, 356 MB result

changes: Poppler text extraction batched per 100-page range instead of one process per page
pdfimages batched per range with -list attribution; per-page fallback on mismatch
whole-document checkpoint on a 100-unit cadence instead of per unit (per-unit files and per-asset sidecars carry resume state)
resume identity from identity.json; completed pages reused without invoking Poppler
CSV/TSV split into bounded chunk units (50k rows / 250k cells per unit) with cell-range provenance
defaults raised: units 20000, timeout 1800 s, output_bytes 512 MiB; streaming size-capped result write
limits_note: CSV result JSON is roughly 12x the input for tiny cells; peak memory grows with the whole document (about 0.9 GB per 700k rows of this shape). Raise limits.memory_bytes/upload_bytes for larger files; a compact/streamed table mode would be needed beyond a few million rows.
